newsitem.title: ERITREA: Anadarko to start Eritrean seismic survey.
newsitem.headline: Anadarko to start Eritrean seismic survey.

text.p: The seismic survey ship hired by American company Anadarko Petroleum Corp to survey its concession in the Eritrean Red Sea has arrived in the port city of Massawa, company officials said on Thursday.

Anadarko is the only petroleum company operating in Eritrea. The company signed an agreement in September 1995 to spend $30 million on an eight-year concession on the 27,4000 square km (10,275 square mile) Zula block, including most of the Dahlak archipelago.
Anadarko Eritrea's General Manager Barclay Collins has previously estimated the survey will take around two to three months.
"After the survey it will take 60 to 90 days to evaluate the data. We plan to start drilling this time next year, in the third quarter," he said in September.
"We will probably spend more money than required and also drill more than one well during the first phase," he added.
The seismic programme will cover most of the concession except the Dahlak archipelago, where the water is too shallow for the ship.
"We will bring a specialised ship to cover the Dahlak archipelago. Maybe this will happen in the first phase (of the eight-year programme)," Collins said.

The Eritrean government is negotiating with a further three or four petroleum companies about concessions in the Red Sea, said Samuel Baire, head of the energy department at the ministry for energy, mining & water resources.
He would not disclose who they are, but said the government had been in negotiations with Mobil Corp for the last two years.
During the 30-year liberation war with Ethiopia, Shell BP, Mobil and Amaco explored what is now the Eritrean Red Sea.
Exploration stopped when a Mobil well blew out in 1969.

Eritrean independence was negotiated during the campaign to oust Ethiopian dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam. Mengistu was toppled in 1991 and Eritrea gained its independence after a national referendum in 1993.
